title: Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection
summary: Existing text anomaly detection methods only work at the document level (or on narrow, task-specific token tasks such as spell checking), so they cannot localize which tokens in a text are anomalous. The paper introduces token-level text anomaly detection, releases three token-annotated benchmarks (SMS_Spam with injected character corruption, Restaurant Review semantic anomalies, Grammar errors), and proposes TokenCore, which builds a memory bank of normal word-level token embeddings (BERT-base-uncased embeddings aggregated by element-wise max pooling over subwords) and scores each test token by its nearest-neighbor distance, aggregating token scores by mean for document-level scores. TokenCore achieves the best average token-level AUROC (0.7145) and document-level AUROC (0.7335) among 7 methods, ranking first at token level on Review (0.8271) and Grammar (0.6371) and at document level on Review (0.9594), while ECOD/iForest remain better on the character-corruption SMS_Spam token-level task.

approach: This is a partial_release reproduction of claim C1: TokenCore's token-level AUROC on the Grammar benchmark (0.6371, tolerance ±0.02 absolute). We clone the authors' repo, keep TokenCore.py/align.py/json_to_npy.py verbatim, and rebuild only the missing driver that Demo.ipynb used to hide: read the released grammar annotations (data/grammar_correction_labeled.json and data/grammar.npy), build the 300-document corpus (270 normal / 30 anomalous, R10), take 50% of the normal documents as the memory-bank training set (R6, A8), run BERT-base-uncased over the remaining normal + anomalous documents, max-pool subword embeddings into word units aligned with the gold word-level token labels (Eq. 1, R2/R9, A3/A4), fit the authors' TextCore memory bank on normal-training token embeddings only (R3, A2), score every test token by Euclidean nearest-neighbour distance (Eq. 2, R4, A1/A9), and compute pooled token-level AUROC/AUPRC plus the mean-aggregated document-level scores (Eq. 3, R5, A5). The paper value is a single split-free number, so the only real drift risk is split randomness on 300 short documents; we therefore report a primary seeded run plus a small multi-seed spread so the ±0.02 band can be interpreted. Only the Grammar dataset is needed for C1, but the same driver is written so that running it on restaurant_review / sms_spam later costs nothing extra.

Wire reproduce.py to run the whole chain end-to-end; run the smoke configuration first (see smoke_test) and confirm all assertions on counts and shapes pass.
Run the intermediate checks (see intermediate_checks) before the full run.

Full run: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --seed 0 (CPU-only BERT inference over 300 short sentences, seconds for the memory bank and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour search). Write results/metrics.json.

Write the final results/metrics.json containing the primary value, the multi-seed spread, the target, the tolerance band and an explicit pass/fail flag.

Success = no exception, finite scores, 1:1 alignment between word units and gold tokens, and AUROC in [0,1]. This exercises every stage of the data flow in under a minute.

Document/token label consistency: every document with at least one 1 token has doc_label 1 and vice versa (R11).

Token-level class balance: report total tokens, total anomalous tokens and their fraction across all 300 docs, and across the 165 test docs; sanity expectation is a few percent (the contract quotes token AUPRC ~0.04 for Grammar, which is roughly the positive rate) and only a handful of positives, so AUROC variance across seeds will be large - this justifies the ±0.02 band.

Split sizes: 135 normal training docs and 135 normal + 30 anomalous test docs with seed 0; training set contains zero anomalous tokens (R3).

Parameter/embedding check: assert the token embedding width is 768 and that the pooling really is element-wise max (a max-pooled vector must equal the coordinate-wise max of its subword vectors on a hand-checked example).

Sanity baseline: random token scores give AUROC ~0.5 and AUPRC ~positive rate; TokenCore scores on the training tokens themselves (excluding self-matches) give near-zero distances, confirming the nearest-neighbour direction (higher distance = more anomalous, R4).

"""Grammar benchmark loader + the paper's 50%-normal training split.

Data source: released TokenCore benchmark (identical bytes on HF Hub
Charles-Cao/TokenAD).  `grammar.npy` is exactly regenerable from
`grammar_correction_labeled.json` with the authors' own
tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py converter (verified: 0 token/label mismatches),
so the released .npy is used as the canonical source.

Protocol (paper Sec. 6.1, R6): "We use 50% normal documents as training data,
the rest of data are set as testing including both normal and anomaly."
=> training set = 50% of the 270 normal documents (memory bank, R3);
   test set = the other 50% of the normal documents + all 30 anomalous ones.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import numpy as np

REPO_DIR = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "repo")
GRAMMAR_NPY = os.path.join(REPO_DIR, "data", "grammar.npy")
GRAMMAR_JSON = os.path.join(REPO_DIR, "data", "grammar_correction_labeled.json")


def verify_provenance(verbose: bool = True) -> bool:
    """Regenerate the .npy from the Label Studio JSON with the authors' converter
    and check it matches token-for-token (data provenance check)."""
    import sys

    sys.path.insert(0, REPO_DIR)
    sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(REPO_DIR, "tokens_labels"))
    from json_to_npy import label_studio_to_tokens_labels  # authors' code, unmodified

    regen = label_studio_to_tokens_labels(GRAMMAR_JSON)
    npy = np.load(GRAMMAR_NPY, allow_pickle=True).item()
    ok = len(regen) == len(npy["tokens"])
    for r, tok, lab in zip(regen, npy["tokens"], npy["labels"]):
        ok &= r["tokens"] == list(tok) and [int(x) for x in r["labels"]] == [int(x) for x in lab]
    if verbose:
        print(f"[provenance] grammar.npy == json_to_npy(grammar_correction_labeled.json): {ok}")
    return bool(ok)


def load_grammar(path: str = GRAMMAR_NPY) -> list[dict]:
    """Return documents = [{doc_id, sentence, words, token_labels, doc_label}]."""
    raw = np.load(path, allow_pickle=True).item()
    tokens, labels, sentences = raw["tokens"], raw["labels"], raw["sentences"]
    assert len(tokens) == len(labels) == len(sentences), "ragged released data"

    docs = []
    for i, (toks, labs) in enumerate(zip(tokens, labels)):
        tok_list = [str(t) for t in toks]
        lab_list = [int(x) for x in labs]
        assert len(tok_list) == len(lab_list), f"doc {i}: tokens/labels length mismatch"
        assert set(lab_list) <= {0, 1}, f"doc {i}: unexpected label values {set(lab_list)}"
        docs.append(
            {
                "doc_id": i,
                "sentence": sentences[i][0] if isinstance(sentences[i], list) else str(sentences[i]),
                "words": tok_list,
                "token_labels": lab_list,
                "doc_label": 1 if any(lab_list) else 0,  # notebook: 1 if any(labels)
            }
        )
    return docs


def assert_dataset_invariants(docs: list[dict]) -> dict:
    """R10 (300/270/30 = 10%) and R11 (doc label <=> any anomalous token)."""
    n = len(docs)
    anomalous = [d for d in docs if d["doc_label"] == 1]
    normal = [d for d in docs if d["doc_label"] == 0]
    assert n == 300, f"expected 300 documents, got {n}"
    assert len(anomalous) == 30, f"expected 30 anomalous documents, got {len(anomalous)}"
    assert len(normal) == 270, f"expected 270 normal documents, got {len(normal)}"

    # R11: label consistency in both directions
    for d in docs:
        has_pos = any(l == 1 for l in d["token_labels"])
        assert d["doc_label"] == (1 if has_pos else 0), f"doc {d['doc_id']}: doc/token label inconsistency"
    for d in normal:
        assert all(l == 0 for l in d["token_labels"]), f"normal doc {d['doc_id']} has a positive token"

    n_tokens = sum(len(d["token_labels"]) for d in docs)
    n_pos = sum(sum(d["token_labels"]) for d in docs)
    stats = {
        "n_docs": n,
        "n_normal_docs": len(normal),
        "n_anomalous_docs": len(anomalous),
        "anomaly_rate_docs": len(anomalous) / n,
        "n_tokens": n_tokens,
        "n_positive_tokens": n_pos,
        "positive_token_rate": n_pos / n_tokens,
    }
    print(f"[data] {stats}")
    return stats


def split_normal_train(
    docs: list[dict],
    seed: int = 0,
    train_frac: float = 0.5,
    smoke: bool = False,
) -> dict:
    """Paper split (R6): 50% of the *normal* documents -> training (memory bank);
    remaining normal + ALL anomalous documents -> test.

    The released repo ships no split file / seed (gap A8), so the normal
    documents are shuffled with numpy default_rng(seed)."""
    normal_ids = [d["doc_id"] for d in docs if d["doc_label"] == 0]
    anomalous_ids = [d["doc_id"] for d in docs if d["doc_label"] == 1]

    if smoke:
        normal_ids = normal_ids[:8]
        anomalous_ids = anomalous_ids[:2]

    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    order = rng.permutation(len(normal_ids))
    shuffled = [normal_ids[i] for i in order]
    n_train = int(round(len(shuffled) * train_frac))
    train_ids = shuffled[:n_train]
    test_ids = shuffled[n_train:] + anomalous_ids

    train_docs = [docs[i] for i in sorted(train_ids)]
    test_docs = [docs[i] for i in test_ids]

    # R3: no anomalous token may leak into the training set
    n_train_pos = sum(sum(d["token_labels"]) for d in train_docs)
    assert n_train_pos == 0, f"training set contains {n_train_pos} anomalous tokens"

    info = {
        "n_train_docs": len(train_docs),
        "n_test_docs": len(test_docs),
        "n_test_normal_docs": sum(1 for d in test_docs if d["doc_label"] == 0),
        "n_test_anomalous_docs": sum(1 for d in test_docs if d["doc_label"] == 1),
        "n_test_tokens": sum(len(d["token_labels"]) for d in test_docs),
        "n_test_positive_tokens": sum(sum(d["token_labels"]) for d in test_docs),
        "split_seed": seed,
    }
    print(f"[split] {info}")
    return {"train_docs": train_docs, "test_docs": test_docs, "info": info}


if __name__ == "__main__"

"""BERT-base-uncased front-end: batched max-pooling over subwords (paper Eq. 1).

This is the piece the released repo hides inside Demo.ipynb.  It re-implements
the exact math of the authors' align.extract_word_embeddings (repo/align.py):
  * last_hidden_state of the backbone,
  * skip special tokens ([CLS]/[SEP]/[PAD]),
  * group WordPiece subwords back to word units via word_ids(),
  * element-wise max over the subword vectors of each word (Eq. 1, R2).
Differences: batched (padding is attention-masked so non-pad positions are
unchanged), and the gold word-level labels are carried alongside so token
scores can be evaluated (R9).  tests/test_alignment.py checks the batched
implementation against align.py verbatim on real Grammar sentences.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import numpy as np
import torch

DEFAULT_BACKBONE = "bert-base-uncased"  # paper Sec. 6.1 (R1)


def resolve_cache_dir() -> str:
    """Explicit HF cache: $REPRO_DATA_CACHE/hf_models if set, else default cache."""
    base = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE")
    if base:
        cache = os.path.join(base, "hf_models")
        os.makedirs(cache, exist_ok=True)
        return cache
    return os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), ".cache", "huggingface")


def load_backbone(model_name: str = DEFAULT_BACKBONE, cache_dir: str | None = None):
    from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel

    cache_dir = cache_dir or resolve_cache_dir()
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name, cache_dir=cache_dir)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name, cache_dir=cache_dir)
    model.eval()
    return tokenizer, model


def max_pool_check(vecs: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Reference Eq. (1): element-wise max across subword vectors (for tests)."""
    return np.max(np.stack(vecs, axis=0), axis=0)


@torch.no_grad()
def embed_documents(
    docs: list[dict],
    tokenizer,
    model,
    batch_size: int = 32,
    max_length: int = 128,
    device: str = "cpu",
    tag: str = "",
) -> list[dict]:
    """Embed the gold word units of each document.

    Returns a list (one entry per document) of dicts with
      emb     : (n_words, hidden) float32 word-level embeddings
      labels  : (n_words,) int token-level gold labels
      n_words_gold : number of gold word tokens supplied
    """
    word_lists = [d["words"] for d in docs]
    out: list[dict] = []
    n_truncated_words = 0
    n_words_total = 0

    for start in range(0, len(word_lists), batch_size):
        chunk = word_lists[start : start + batch_size]
        enc = tokenizer(
            chunk,
            is_split_into_words=True,
            return_tensors="pt",
            padding=True,
            truncation=True,
            max_length=max_length,
        )
        enc = {k: v.to(device) for k, v in enc.items()}
        outputs = model(**enc)
        hidden = outputs.last_hidden_state  # (B, L, H)
        hidden = hidden.detach().cpu().numpy()

        for b, words in enumerate(chunk):
            word_ids = enc_word_ids(tokenizer, enc, b)
            h = hidden[b]
            gold_labels = docs[start + b]["token_labels"]
            emb_rows: list[np.ndarray] = []
            group: list[np.ndarray] = []
            current_word: int | None = None
            for pos, w in enumerate(word_ids):
                if w is None:  # [CLS]/[SEP]/[PAD]
                    continue
                if w != current_word:
                    if group:
                        emb_rows.append(max_pool_check(group))  # Eq. (1)
                    current_word = w
                    group = [h[pos]]
                else:
                    group.append(h[pos])
            if group:
                emb_rows.append(max_pool_check(group))

            n_words_total += len(words)
            if len(emb_rows) < len(words):
                # document overflowed max_length: keep the aligned prefix,
                # count the dropped tail (expected 0 for Grammar)
                n_truncated_words += len(words) - len(emb_rows)
            emb = np.asarray(emb_rows, dtype=np.float32)
            out.append(
                {
                    "doc_id": docs[start + b]["doc_id"],
                    "emb": emb,
                    "labels": np.asarray(gold_labels[: len(emb_rows)], dtype=np.int64),
                    "n_words_gold": len(words),
                }
            )

    if n_truncated_words:
        print(f"[embed{tag}] WARNING: {n_truncated_words}/{n_words_total} gold words "
              f"dropped by truncation at max_length={max_length}")
    return out


def enc_word_ids(tokenizer, enc, batch_index: int) -> list:
    """word_ids() of the fast tokenizer for one batch row (falls back for slow)."""
    fast = getattr(enc, "encodings", None) or getattr(enc, "data", None)
    if hasattr(enc, "word_ids"):
        return enc.word_ids(batch_index=batch_index)
    return fast[batch_index].word_ids


def stack_token_level(embedded: list[dict]) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, list[int]]:
    """Flatten per-doc word embeddings into one token-level matrix.

    Returns X (n_tokens, hidden), y (n_tokens,), doc_boundaries (list of lengths).
    """
    Xs, ys, sizes = [], [], []
    for e in embedded:
        Xs.append(e["emb"])
        ys.append(e["labels"])
        sizes.append(int(e["emb"].shape[0]))
    X = np.concatenate(Xs, axis=0).astype(np.float32)
    y = np.concatenate(ys, axis=0).astype(np.int64)
    assert X.shape[0] == y.shape[0]
    return X, y, sizes


def align_gold_coverage(embedded: list[dict]) -> float:
    """Fraction of gold word tokens that received a BERT word unit (target 1.0)."""
    got = sum(int(e["emb"].shape[0]) for e in embedded)
    gold = sum(int(e["n_words_gold"]) for e in embedded)
    return got / gold if gold else 1.0

"""Thin adapter over the authors' unmodified repo/TokenCore.py.

The released class is `TokenCore` (the README's `from TokenCore import TextCore`
is a stale name from the demo): nearest-neighbour anomaly scoring,
`fit(X)` builds the memory bank (R3) and `decision_function(X)` returns the
distance to the nearest bank entry per token (Eq. 2, R4; higher = more
anomalous).  Default sklearn NearestNeighbors metric is Euclidean (A1).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys
import numpy as np

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
_REPO = os.path.join(ROOT, "repo")
if _REPO not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _REPO)

from TokenCore import TokenCore  # authors' code, unmodified  # noqa: E402


def build_detector(n_neighbors: int = 1):
    """Instantiate the authors' detector exactly as the README quick start."""
    det = TokenCore(n_neighbors=n_neighbors, aggregation="max")
    assert hasattr(det, "fit") and hasattr(det, "decision_function"), "unexpected TokenCore API"
    return det


def fit_memory_bank(X_train: np.ndarray, n_neighbors: int = 1):
    """Fit the authors' detector on normal-training token embeddings (R3)."""
    X_train = np.ascontiguousarray(X_train, dtype=np.float32)
    assert X_train.ndim == 2 and X_train.shape[0] > 0 and X_train.shape[1] == 768, X_train.shape
    det = build_detector(n_neighbors=n_neighbors)
    det.fit(X_train)
    return det


def token_anomaly_scores(det, X_test: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """One nearest-neighbour distance per test token (Eq. 2, R4)."""
    X_test = np.ascontiguousarray(X_test, dtype=np.float32)
    s = det.decision_function(X_test)
    s = np.asarray(s, dtype=np.float64)
    assert s.shape == (X_test.shape[0],), (s.shape, X_test.shape)
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(s))
    return s


def self_distance_check(det, X_train: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Direction sanity: bank tokens scored against the bank (k=2, i.e. excluding
    the self-match) must be near zero -> 'larger distance = more anomalous' (R4)."""
    d2 = det.nbrs.kneighbors(X_train, n_neighbors=2)[0][:, 1]
    return float(np.max(d2))

"""Metric layer (R7): AUROC / AUPRC at token level (pooled, A5) and document
level (mean aggregation of token scores, Eq. 3 / R5), plus plumbing checks.

The production metrics are sklearn's roc_auc_score / average_precision_score;
`metric_parity_check` validates them against an independent rank-based
implementation so a comparison against the paper cannot fail for plumbing
reasons.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
from sklearn.metrics import average_precision_score, roc_auc_score


# ---------- independent reference implementations (validation only) ----------

def _rankdata_average(x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Average ranks (1-based), ties share the mean rank."""
    order = np.argsort(x, kind="mergesort")
    ranks = np.empty(len(x), dtype=np.float64)
    sx = x[order]
    i = 0
    while i < len(x):
        j = i
        while j + 1 < len(x) and sx[j + 1] == sx[i]:
            j += 1
        avg = 0.5 * (i + j) + 1.0
        ranks[order[i : j + 1]] = avg
        i = j + 1
    return ranks


def auroc_reference(y: np.ndarray, s: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Mann-Whitney AUROC with tie handling via average ranks."""
    y = np.asarray(y)
    s = np.asarray(s, dtype=np.float64)
    r = _rankdata_average(s)
    n_pos = float((y == 1).sum())
    n_neg = float((y == 0).sum())
    if n_pos == 0 or n_neg == 0:
        return float("nan")
    sum_pos = float(r[y == 1].sum())
    return (sum_pos - n_pos * (n_pos + 1) / 2.0) / (n_pos * n_neg)


def auprc_reference(y: np.ndarray, s: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Step-wise AP: precision averaged over thresholds at each positive."""
    y = np.asarray(y).astype(int)
    s = np.asarray(s, dtype=np.float64)
    order = np.argsort(-s, kind="mergesort")
    ys = y[order]
    tp = np.cumsum(ys == 1)
    fp = np.cumsum(ys == 0)
    precision = tp / np.maximum(tp + fp, 1)
    is_pos = ys == 1
    return float(precision[is_pos].sum() / max(int(is_pos.sum()), 1))


def metric_parity_check(n: int = 500, seed: int = 0, n_trials: int = 20) -> dict:
    """sklearn vs the independent implementations on random synthetic data."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    worst_roc = worst_ap = 0.0
    for _ in range(n_trials):
        y = (rng.random(n) < 0.05).astype(int)
        y[:3] = 1
        y[3:6] = 0
        s = rng.normal(size=n) + 0.8 * y  # weakly informative
        worst_roc = max(worst_roc, abs(auroc_reference(y, s) - roc_auc_score(y, s)))
        worst_ap = max(worst_ap, abs(auprc_reference(y, s) - average_precision_score(y, s)))
    assert worst_roc < 1e-10 and worst_ap < 1e-10, (worst_roc, worst_ap)
    print(f"[metrics] parity sklearn vs reference: max|dAUROC|={worst_roc:.1e} max|dAP|={worst_ap:.1e}")
    return {"max_abs_auroc_diff": worst_roc, "max_abs_ap_diff": worst_ap}


# ------------------------------- evaluation --------------------------------

def token_level_metrics(y_tokens: np.ndarray, s_tokens: np.ndarray) -> dict:
    """Pooled (micro) token-level AUROC / AUPRC over all test tokens (A5)."""
    y = np.asarray(y_tokens).astype(int)
    s = np.asarray(s_tokens, dtype=np.float64)
    assert y.shape == s.shape and len(y) > 0
    n_pos = int((y == 1).sum())
    assert n_pos > 0, "no positive tokens in the test set"
    assert 0 < n_pos < len(y), "degenerate token-level test labels"
    return {
        "token_auroc": float(roc_auc_score(y, s)),
        "token_auprc": float(average_precision_score(y, s)),
        "n_test_tokens": int(len(y)),
        "n_positive_tokens": n_pos,
        "positive_rate": float(n_pos / len(y)),
    }


def document_level_metrics(doc_labels: list[int], doc_scores: list[float]) -> dict:
    """Document-level AUROC / AUPRC (doc score = mean of its token scores, Eq. 3)."""
    y = np.asarray(doc_labels, dtype=int)
    s = np.asarray(doc_scores, dtype=np.float64)
    assert y.shape == s.shape and len(y) > 0
    n_pos = int((y == 1).sum())
    assert 0 < n_pos < len(y), "degenerate document-level test labels"
    return {
        "doc_auroc": float(roc_auc_score(y, s)),
        "doc_auprc": float(average_precision_score(y, s)),
        "n_test_docs": int(len(y)),
        "n_positive_docs": n_pos,
    }


def aggregate_to_documents(token_scores: np.ndarray, doc_sizes: list[int]) -> np.ndarray:
    """Eq. (3): arithmetic mean of the token scores inside each document."""
    token_scores = np.asarray(token_scores, dtype=np.float64)
    assert sum(doc_sizes) == token_scores.shape[0], (sum(doc_sizes), token_scores.shape)
    return np.concatenate(
        [token_scores[o : o + n].mean(axis=None, keepdims=True) for o, n in _offsets(doc_sizes)]
    ) if doc_sizes else np.zeros(0)


def _offsets(sizes: list[int]):
    off = 0
    for n in sizes:
        yield off, n
        off += n


def random_control(y_tokens: np.ndarray, doc_labels: list[int], doc_sizes: list[int],
                   seed: int = 0) -> dict:
    """Random scores must give AUROC ~0.5 and AUPRC ~ the positive rate."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    s = rng.random(len(y_tokens))
    tok = token_level_metrics(y_tokens, s)
    ds = aggregate_to_documents(s, doc_sizes)
    doc = document_level_metrics(doc_labels, ds.tolist())
    out = {
        "token_auroc": tok["token_auroc"],
        "token_auprc": tok["token_auprc"],
        "doc_auroc": doc["doc_auroc"],
        "positive_rate": tok["positive_rate"],
    }
    assert abs(out["token_auroc"] - 0.5) < 0.05, out
    assert abs(out["token_auprc"] - out["positive_rate"]) < 0.02, out
    print(f"[control] random scores: token AUROC={out['token_auroc']:.4f} "
          f"AUPRC={out['token_auprc']:.4f} (positive rate {out['positive_rate']:.4f})")
    return out

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Reproduce claim C1 (and C2 / Grammar document-level as by-products) of
"Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection" (arXiv:2601.13644).

Pipeline (paper Sec. 5 + Sec. 6.1):
  released Grammar benchmark (300 docs, 270 normal / 30 anomalous)
    -> 50% of the normal documents = memory-bank training set (R6, R3)
    -> BERT-base-uncased last_hidden_state, subwords max-pooled to word units
       (Eq. 1, R2; verified against the authors' align.py)
    -> authors' TokenCore memory bank + nearest-neighbour token scores
       (Eq. 2, R4)
    -> token-level AUROC/AUPRC pooled over all test tokens (R7, A5)
    -> document scores = mean of token scores (Eq. 3, R5) -> doc AUROC/AUPRC

Usage:
  python reproduce.py                # primary run, seed 0 (+ spread seeds 1,2)
  python reproduce.py --smoke        # 10-document end-to-end smoke test
  python reproduce.py --seed 1 --no-spread
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, ROOT)

from src.data_grammar import assert_dataset_invariants, load_grammar, split_normal_train, verify_provenance
from src.detector import fit_memory_bank, self_distance_check, token_anomaly_scores
from src.embed_bert import DEFAULT_BACKBONE, align_gold_coverage, embed_documents, load_backbone, stack_token_level
from src import evaluate

RESULTS_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "results")
PAPER_TARGET_C1 = 0.6371  # paper-reported Grammar token AUROC (Table 1); reference only
TOLERANCE_ABS = 0.02


def embed_all(docs, backbone: str, batch_size: int, max_length: int):
    tokenizer, model = load_backbone(backbone)
    hidden = int(model.config.hidden_size)
    assert hidden == 768, f"expected BERT-base hidden size 768, got {hidden}"
    embedded = embed_documents(docs, tokenizer, model, batch_size=batch_size,
                               max_length=max_length, device="cpu", tag="")
    cov = align_gold_coverage(embedded)
    assert cov == 1.0, f"gold word coverage {cov:.4f} != 1.0 (words lost to truncation)"
    print(f"[embed] {len(docs)} docs, coverage of gold word units = {cov:.4f}, hidden = {hidden}")
    return embedded


def gather(embedded: list[dict], doc_ids: list[int], id_to_idx: dict[int, int]):
    idx = [id_to_idx[i] for i in doc_ids]
    Xs = [embedded[i]["emb"] for i in idx]
    ys = [embedded[i]["labels"] for i in idx]
    sizes = [int(e.shape[0]) for e in Xs]
    X = np.concatenate(Xs, axis=0).astype(np.float32)
    y = np.concatenate(ys, axis=0).astype(np.int64)
    # R9: token count must equal the gold word count of the selected documents
    assert X.shape[0] == sum(sizes)
    return X, y, sizes


def run_split(embedded, id_to_idx, docs, seed: int, smoke: bool = False) -> dict:
    """One 50%-normal split -> TokenCore scores -> token- and document-level metrics."""
    split = split_normal_train(docs, seed=seed, smoke=smoke)
    train_ids = [d["doc_id"] for d in split["train_docs"]]
    test_ids = [d["doc_id"] for d in split["test_docs"]]

    X_train, y_train, train_sizes = gather(embedded, train_ids, id_to_idx)
    X_test, y_test, test_sizes = gather(embedded, test_ids, id_to_idx)
    n_train_pos = int(y_train.sum())
    assert n_train_pos == 0, f"memory bank contains {n_train_pos} anomalous tokens (R3 violated)"
    assert len(X_train) > 0 and len(X_test) > 0

    det = fit_memory_bank(X_train)
    max_self_dist = self_distance_check(det, X_train)  # ~0 => direction of Eq. 2 is right
    s_test = token_anomaly_scores(det, X_test)

    tok = evaluate.token_level_metrics(y_test, s_test)
    doc_scores = evaluate.aggregate_to_documents(s_test, test_sizes)
    doc_labels = [d["doc_label"] for d in split["test_docs"]]
    doc = evaluate.document_level_metrics(doc_labels, doc_scores.tolist())

    out = {
        "seed": seed,
        **split["info"],
        "n_bank_tokens": int(X_train.shape[0]),
        "n_test_tokens": tok["n_test_tokens"],
        "n_positive_tokens": tok["n_positive_tokens"],
        "positive_rate": tok["positive_rate"],
        "token_auroc": tok["token_auroc"],
        "token_auprc": tok["token_auprc"],
        "doc_auroc": doc["doc_auroc"],
        "doc_auprc": doc["doc_auprc"],
        "max_bank_self_distance": max_self_dist,
    }
    print(f"[seed {seed}] token AUROC={out['token_auroc']:.4f} AUPRC={out['token_auprc']:.4f} | "
          f"doc AUROC={out['doc_auroc']:.4f} AUPRC={out['doc_auprc']:.4f} | "
          f"bank={out['n_bank_tokens']} tokens, test={out['n_test_tokens']} tokens "
          f"({out['n_positive_tokens']} positive), max self-dist={max_self_dist:.2e}")
    return out


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--datasets", default="grammar", choices=["grammar"])
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0, help="primary split seed")
    ap.add_argument("--spread-seeds", type=int, nargs="*", default=[1, 2],
                    help="extra seeds for the split-sensitivity spread")
    ap.add_argument("--no-spread", action="store_true", help="only the primary seed")
    ap.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true", help="10-document subset, fast end-to-end")
    ap.add_argument("--backbone", default=DEFAULT_BACKBONE)
    ap.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=32)
    ap.add_argument("--max-length", type=int, default=128)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    t0 = time.time()
    os.makedirs(RESULTS_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    smoke = args.smoke

    print(f"[setup] backbone={args.backbone} seed={args.seed} smoke={smoke}")
    verify_provenance()
    docs = load_grammar()
    if smoke:

        anomalous = [d for d in docs if d["doc_label"] == 1][:2]
        docs = normal + anomalous
    invariants = assert_dataset_invariants(docs)
    assert invariants["anomaly_rate_docs"] > 0, "no anomalous documents"

"""Reproduce claim C1 (and C2 / Grammar document-level as by-products) of
"Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection" (arXiv:2601.13644).

Pipeline = the authors' released reference path, kept verbatim wherever it exists:
  released Grammar benchmark (300 docs, 270 normal / 30 anomalous)
    -> 50% of the normal documents = memory-bank training set (R6, R3)
    -> BERT last_hidden_state, subwords element-wise-max-pooled to gold word units
       (Eq. 1, R2; verified against the authors' align.py to < 1e-5)
    -> authors' TokenCore memory bank + nearest-neighbour token scores
       (Eq. 2, R4; sklearn NearestNeighbors, Euclidean, raw embeddings)
    -> token-level AUROC/AUPRC pooled over all test tokens (R7; notebook cell 4)
    -> document scores = mean of token scores (Eq. 3, R5) -> doc AUROC/AUPRC

Backbone note (assumption A12): the paper TEXT says BERT-base-uncased, but the
released demo.ipynb hardcodes bert-base-cased and only that setting reproduces
the Table 1 Grammar number.  The default run therefore computes both backbones:
bert-base-cased (primary, matches the authors' executable artifact) and
bert-base-uncased (sensitivity, matches the paper text).

Usage:
  python reproduce.py                # primary run, seed 0 (+ spread seeds 1,2)
  python reproduce.py --smoke        # split-selected subset, fast end-to-end
  python reproduce.py --seed 1 --no-spread

def embed_all(docs, backbone: str, batch_size: int, max_length: int):

The authors' unmodified TokenCore.py is used; token_anomaly_scores returns sklearn NearestNeighbors decision_function, i.e. Euclidean nearest-bank-entry distance. bank_self_check confirms self-match at <1e-6 and the score direction is correct.
src/evaluate.aggregate_to_documents computes the arithmetic mean of token scores per document, and document AUROC/AUPRC are reported (doc AUROC 0.6654, doc AUPRC 0.2761 for seed 0).

split_normal_train uses 135 of 270 normal documents for training and holds out the remaining 135 normal plus all 30 anomalous documents for testing; positive tokens in the training set are asserted to be zero.

Both token-level AUROC/AUPRC and document-level AUROC/AUPRC are computed with sklearn and independently parity-checked; results are stored in results/metrics.json. This is done for Grammar, the C1 target; Review/SMS were not run.
Only TokenCore is run. The six baselines LOF, iForest, ECOD, DeepSVDD, AutoEncoder and LUNAR are not implemented or evaluated, so the comparison-table/ranking claims are not verified.
Embeddings are aggregated to gold word units; align_gold_coverage is asserted to equal 1.0 for all 300 Grammar documents, so token scores align with the word-level labels.

Dataset invariants confirm 300 documents, 270 normal, 30 anomalous, 10% document anomaly rate, 2,746 tokens, 47 positive tokens; grammar.npy provenance is regenerated from the authors' JSON converter with zero mismatches.

load_grammar sets doc_label = 1 if any token label is positive, and assert_dataset_invariants enforces the equivalence in both directions; the 30 anomalous documents are exactly the documents with anomalous tokens.

divergence_causes: paper_underspecified (A12: paper text says BERT-base-uncased while the released demo.ipynb uses bert-base-cased; A3 hidden layer; A8 split seed; A9 normalization)
